name: Autosomal Dominant Otospondylomegaepiphyseal Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for AD OSMED

criteria.description: Characteristic facial features including midface hypoplasia and prominent forehead
Conductive hearing loss due to otosclerosis confirmed by audiometry and imaging
Radiographic evidence of epiphyseal and metaphyseal abnormalities with enlarged epiphyses
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the COL11A2 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic facial dysmorphism, conductive hearing loss due to otosclerosis, skeletal abnormalities on imaging, and identification of COL11A2 mutation or positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is strongly recommended to confirm diagnosis. Differential diagnosis includes other collagenopathies and skeletal dysplasias.

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing COL11A2 pathogenic variants
imaging: Radiographs showing enlarged epiphyses and metaphyseal abnormalities
CT or MRI of temporal bones showing otosclerosis
other: Audiometric testing confirming conductive hearing loss
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

redFlags: Progressive conductive hearing loss in early childhood
Severe skeletal deformities causing functional impairment
Family history of similar skeletal and hearing abnormalities
references: Murray JC, et al. Otospondylomegaepiphyseal Dysplasia: Clinical and Molecular Characterization. Am J Med Genet. 1996.
